root_cause.text: The page recycling for XDP_DROP was unconditionally removed from emac_run_xdp() to avoid conflicts with AF_XDP zero-copy mode, but this caused a memory leak in non-zero-copy mode because the pages were never returned to the page pool after an XDP_DROP verdict.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Page recycling was removed from the XDP_DROP path in emac_run_xdp() to avoid conflicts with AF_XDP zero-copy mode... However, this causes a memory leak when running XDP programs that drop packets in non-zero-copy mode (standard page pool mode). The pages are never returned to the page pool, leading to OOM conditions." The patch adds recycling in the caller (`emac_rx_packet()`) for the `ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED` case, confirming that the missing recycling was the bug.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix buffer leak by recycling the page when XDP consumes a packet in the EMAC RX path.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block that checks if the result of emac_run_xdp is ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED; if so, it calls page_pool_recycle_direct(pool, page) and jumps to the requeue label.
intent_record.how: When XDP consumes a packet (e.g., XDP_DROP), the driver now directly recycles the page to the page pool, ensuring proper buffer reuse instead of falling through to the generic requeue path that may not recycle the page.
